column2: What are the top attractions to see in Rome
column3: The Colosseum, Roman Forum, Pantheon, Trevi Fountain, and Vatican City.

column2: What is the best area to explore for history in Rome?
column3: The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill are great for history lovers.

column2: Where should I go for art in Rome?
column3: Visit the Vatican Museums and the Sistine Chapel.

column2: Should I book dinner in advance in Rome?
column3: Booking is recommended for popular spots, especially on weekends

column2: Do I need to tip in Rome restaurants?
column3: Service is usually included; a small tip is optional.

column2: Is tap water safe to drink in Rome?
column3: Tap water is generally safe; you can also ask for bottled water.

column2: Do restaurants charge for bread or table service?
column3: Some places add a small service or bread charge; check the menu.

column2: Do you offer delivery or only pickup?
column3: We offer both delivery and pickup.

column2: How long does delivery usually take?
column3: Delivery typically takes 30 to 45 minutes depending on your location.

column2: Is there a minimum order amount for delivery?
column3: Yes, a minimum order of 15 euros is required for delivery.

column2: Can I customize my pizza toppings?
column3: Yes, you can add or remove toppings for an extra charge where applicable.

column2: Do you have any deals for large orders?
column3: We offer a 10% discount on orders of 3 or more pizzas.

column2: What's the price range for your pizzas?
column3: Our pizzas range from 8 to 16 euros depending on size and toppings.

column2: Do you have gluten-free crust options?
Can I order a half-and-half pizza with two flavors?
column3: Yes, we offer half-and-half pizzas at a small additional cost.

column2: What drinks do you have available?
column3: We offer soft drinks, water, and a selection of Italian beers and wines.

column2: How do I get from Rome Fiumicino airport to the city center?
column3: You can take the Leonardo Express train, a taxi, or a shuttle bus.

column2: How long does the train from the airport take?
column3: The Leonardo Express takes about 32 minutes to Termini station.

column2: Is the Rome public transport system easy to use for tourists?
column3: Yes, buses, metro, and trams are tourist-friendly with a single ticket system.

column2: Do I need to buy separate tickets for metro and bus?
column3: No, a standard ticket is valid across metro, bus, and tram within 100 minutes.

column2: What's the best time of year to visit Rome?
column3: Spring (April-May) and Fall (September-October) offer pleasant weather with fewer crowds.

column2: Is Rome very crowded in the summer?
column3: Yes, July and August are peak tourist season with high crowds and heat.

column2: Should I avoid visiting in winter?
column3: Winter is quieter and cooler, but most attractions remain open.

column2: Do I need to book Colosseum tickets in advance?
column3: Yes, booking in advance is strongly recommended to avoid long queues.

column2: Can you recommend a good area to stay in Rome?
column3: Trastevere and the historic center near the Pantheon are popular choices.

column2: Is Trastevere a safe area for tourists?
column3: Yes, Trastevere is generally considered safe and popular with visitors.

column2: How far is Trastevere from the Colosseum?
column3: It's about a 25-30 minute walk, or a short taxi/bus ride.

column2: Do you offer vegan pizza options?
column3: Yes, we offer a vegan Margherita with plant-based cheese.

column2: What toppings are included in your vegan pizza?
column3: Tomato sauce, plant-based cheese, basil, and cherry tomatoes.

column2: Is the vegan cheese available on any pizza?
column3: Yes, you can substitute vegan cheese on any pizza for an extra charge.

column2: Do you label allergens on your menu?
column3: Yes, common allergens are listed next to each menu item.

column2: What's the dress code for visiting the Vatican Museums?
column3: Shoulders and knees should be covered; no sleeveless tops or short shorts.

column2: How much time should I plan for the Vatican Museums?
column3: Plan for at least 3 hours to see the main highlights, including the Sistine Chapel.

column2: Are the Vatican Museums open on Sundays?
column3: They're open on the last Sunday of the month for free entry; otherwise closed on Sundays.

column2: Can I buy skip-the-line tickets online?
column3: Yes, skip-the-line tickets are available on the official Vatican Museums website.
